overall: Atlanta is tracking a warm mid-June afternoon with the running max already reaching 84.9°F at 14:05 ET. Temperatures have climbed steadily through the morning and early afternoon under partly sunny skies (FEW clouds, ceiling ~853m), though the current reading of 84.2°F is fractionally below the running max, suggesting a brief plateau. Active severe weather and flash flood activity is confined to southeastern Georgia and the Florida panhandle — well south of Atlanta — and poses no direct immediate suppression risk to the metro high.
forecast_obs_notes: The NWP models are tightly clustered: ECMWF=84.9°F, NBM=84.8°F, HRRR=84.1°F — essentially capping near the current running max. max_temp_prediction: With the running max already at 84.9°F, positive 30-minute velocity (+3.6°F/hr), and peak timing models pointing to 15–17h ET, modest additional warming is plausible before the afternoon convective window (NWS 20% PoP after 2pm) could cap or suppress further gains. Balancing the tightly clustered NWP guidance near 84.1–84.9°F against NWS/META support for 86°F and remaining diurnal heating, a final high around 85.5–86°F is most likely, with moderate confidence; the primary downside risk is early afternoon storm development capping the day near the current running max.
